name: MHT-CET (PCM)
fullName: Maharashtra Common Entrance Test – PCM Group
conductingBody: State Common Entrance Test Cell, Maharashtra
frequency: Once a year, with two attempts proposed for the 2027 cycle
approxCandidates: ≈4–5 lakh PCM-group registrations per year (2025–26 cycles; ≈7+ lakh across PCM and PCB)
eligibility: Class 12 (or appearing) with Physics, Mathematics and Chemistry/Biology/Technical vocational subject; domicile rules apply for state-quota seats

The detailed information brochure, registration window and exact PCM dates had not been published as of 10 Oct 2026.

importantDates.date: 15 Dec 2026 – 15 Jan 2027 (window per CET Cell notice; exact PCM dates awaited)

notification.source: https://articles.findmycollege.com/news/mht-cet-2027-first-attempt-from-december-15-registration-expected-in-october/ (news report of CET Cell notice; confirm on cetcell.mahacet.org)

pattern.notes: Physics and Chemistry are one combined 90-minute paper (+1 each); Mathematics is a separate 90-minute paper with +2 per correct answer. No negative marking. About 80% of questions are from Maharashtra Class 12 syllabus and 20% from selected Class 11 chapters. Multi-shift exam; percentile scores are normalised.

trendAnalysis.summary: The paper is speed-oriented and mostly direct, with Maharashtra State Board (HSC) textbooks as the base. Mathematics carries double marks and is the deciding section; calculus (differentiation, integration, definite integrals, differential equations), vectors/3D, probability distributions and mathematical logic are the highest-yield areas. Physics stresses Class 12 chapters such as rotational dynamics, wave optics, electrostatics, current electricity and EMI with formula-based numericals. Chemistry is largely NCERT/HSC-text based, with solid state, solutions, electrochemistry, coordination and named organic reactions appearing every shift. Difficulty varies by shift (easy to moderate overall), so normalised percentiles matter.

pyqBlueprint.method: Compiled from the State CET Cell's officially published MHT CET PCM question papers/response sheets (multi-shift, April–May 2024 and 2025, 2026 cycle) as summarised in public shift-wise analyses (Careers360, CollegeDost, CollegeDekho), which web search confirmed for chapter emphasis (integration and 3D geometry in Maths; numerical-heavy Physics; p-block, solutions, kinetics and organic in Chemistry; roughly 80% Class 12 / 20% Class 11 Maharashtra syllabus). Full papers could not be fetched, so the recurring direct-formula patterns and traps were written from the drafter's own knowledge of these papers and the Maharashtra State Board textbooks.

resources.notes: The CET Cell does not publish full question papers for public download; candidates can view their own question paper, responses and provisional answer key during the objection window after the exam. Syllabus, sample/mock test links and notices appear on cetcell.mahacet.org. Shift-wise 'previous papers' sold or posted online are memory-based reconstructions, not official.

questions.question: A horizontal disc rotates freely about its vertical axis at 30 rpm. An identical disc, initially at rest, is gently placed coaxially on it and both rotate together. The common angular speed is
questions.explanation: Angular momentum is conserved: Iω = 2Iω' ⇒ ω' = 15 rpm.

questions.question: The radius of gyration of a solid sphere of radius R about any diameter is
A road of radius 50 m is banked such that tan θ = 0.2. The speed at which a vehicle can negotiate the curve without relying on friction is (g = 10 m/s²)
Eight identical rain drops, each falling with terminal velocity v, coalesce into one big drop. The terminal velocity of the big drop is
questions.explanation: Volume conserved: R³ = 8r³ ⇒ R = 2r. Terminal velocity ∝ r², so v' = 4v.

questions.question: The excess pressure inside a soap bubble of radius 1 cm (surface tension 0.03 N/m) is
questions.explanation: A soap bubble has two surfaces: ΔP = 4T/r = 4 × 0.03/0.01 = 12 Pa.

questions.question: If the absolute temperature of a black body is doubled, the total power it radiates becomes
questions.explanation: Stefan–Boltzmann law: P ∝ T⁴ ⇒ 2⁴ = 16.

questions.question: A diatomic ideal gas (γ = 1.4) at 300 K is compressed adiabatically to 1/32 of its initial volume. Its final temperature is
A mass on a spring oscillates with period T. If it is instead attached to two such identical springs connected in series, the period becomes
questions.explanation: Series: k_eff = k/2. T ∝ 1/√k ⇒ T' = √2 T.

questions.question: Tuning fork A (256 Hz) produces 4 beats per second with fork B. When B is loaded with a little wax, the beat frequency increases to 6 per second. The original frequency of B was
questions.explanation: B is 252 or 260 Hz. Loading lowers B's frequency; beats increase only if B was below A: 252 → lower gives more beats. So B = 252 Hz.

questions.question: Light of wavelength 600 nm falls normally on a single slit of width 0.3 mm. The width of the central maximum on a screen 2 m away is
The Brewster angle for a transparent medium of refractive index √3 is
questions.explanation: tan i_p = μ = √3 ⇒ i_p = 60°.

questions.question: Three capacitors of 2 μF, 3 μF and 6 μF are connected in series. The equivalent capacitance is
A uniform potentiometer wire 10 m long has a steady potential difference of 2 V across it. The balancing length for a cell of emf 1.5 V is
questions.explanation: Potential gradient = 2/10 = 0.2 V/m. Balancing length = 1.5/0.2 = 7.5 m.

questions.topic: Magnetic Fields due to Electric Current
questions.question: Two long parallel wires 1 m apart in vacuum each carry a current of 1 A. The force per metre length between them is
questions.explanation: F/l = μ₀I₁I₂/(2πd) = 4π×10⁻⁷ × 1 × 1/(2π × 1) = 2 × 10⁻⁷ N/m (the definition of the ampere).

questions.question: A coil of 500 turns and area 0.01 m² is held perpendicular to a magnetic field that decreases uniformly from 0.2 T to zero in 0.1 s. The magnitude of the induced emf is
A series LCR circuit has L = 2 H, C = 2 μF and R = 10 Ω. The quality factor of the circuit at resonance is
Light of wavelength 400 nm falls on a metal of work function 2.5 eV. The maximum kinetic energy of the emitted photoelectrons is approximately (hc = 1240 eV nm)
questions.explanation: Photon energy = 1240/400 = 3.1 eV. K_max = 3.1 − 2.5 = 0.6 eV.

questions.question: In Bohr's model, the ratio of the speed of the electron in the first orbit of hydrogen to the speed of light is approximately
questions.explanation: v₁ = e²/(2ε₀h) ≈ 2.19 × 10⁶ m/s; v₁/c ≈ 1/137 (the fine-structure constant).

questions.question: For a transistor, the common-base current gain α is 0.98. Its common-emitter current gain β is

questions.topic: Motion in a Plane & Laws of Motion (XI)
questions.question: A projectile is fired so as to achieve the maximum horizontal range of 100 m on level ground. The maximum height reached is
questions.explanation: Max range at 45°: R = u²/g. Height H = u² sin²45°/(2g) = R/4 = 25 m.

questions.question: The packing efficiency of a body-centred cubic (bcc) lattice is approximately
questions.explanation: In bcc, 2 atoms per cell with 4r = √3 a; packing fraction = √3π/8 ≈ 0.68.

questions.question: An element (molar mass 60 g mol⁻¹) crystallises in an fcc lattice with edge length 400 pm. Its density is approximately (N_A = 6.022 × 10²³ mol⁻¹)
The osmotic pressure of a 0.1 M aqueous glucose solution at 300 K is (R = 0.0821 L atm K⁻¹ mol⁻¹)
questions.explanation: π = CRT = 0.1 × 0.0821 × 300 ≈ 2.46 atm (glucose does not dissociate).

questions.question: The pH of a 0.001 M aqueous NaOH solution at 25 °C is
The degree of dissociation of 0.1 M acetic acid (Ka = 1.8 × 10⁻⁵) is approximately
For N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) → 2NH₃(g) at temperature T, ΔH − ΔU equals
questions.explanation: ΔH = ΔU + Δn_gRT with Δn_g = 2 − 4 = −2, so ΔH − ΔU = −2RT.

questions.question: The mass of copper deposited from CuSO₄ solution by passing 0.5 faraday of electricity is (Cu = 63.5)
The rate constant of a first-order reaction is 0.0693 min⁻¹. Its half-life is
Which xenon compound has a square pyramidal shape?
questions.explanation: XeOF₄ has 5 bond pairs and 1 lone pair (octahedral arrangement) ⇒ square pyramidal. XeF₄ is square planar, XeO₃ pyramidal, XeF₂ linear.

questions.question: The oxidation state of sulphur in peroxodisulphuric acid (H₂S₂O₈) is
questions.explanation: H₂S₂O₈ contains one peroxide (–O–O–) link with O at −1. 2(+1) + 2x + 6(−2) + 2(−1) = 0 ⇒ x = +6. (Assuming all O as −2 wrongly gives +7.)

questions.question: Which of the following ions is colourless in aqueous solution?
questions.explanation: Sc³⁺ is 3d⁰, so no d–d transition is possible. Ti³⁺ (d¹), Cu²⁺ (d⁹) and Ni²⁺ (d⁸) are coloured.

questions.question: The IUPAC name of K₃[Fe(CN)₆] is
questions.explanation: Anionic complex ⇒ metal named 'ferrate'; CN⁻ is 'cyanido'; Fe is +3 since 3(+1) + x + 6(−1) = 0.

questions.question: Chlorobenzene and methyl chloride are treated with sodium in dry ether. The main product is
questions.explanation: Wurtz–Fittig reaction couples the aryl and alkyl groups: C₆H₅Cl + CH₃Cl + 2Na → C₆H₅CH₃ + 2NaCl.

questions.question: Phenol on treatment with chloroform and aqueous NaOH, followed by acidification, gives mainly
questions.explanation: Reimer–Tiemann reaction introduces –CHO at the ortho position to give 2-hydroxybenzaldehyde (salicylaldehyde).

questions.question: Which of the following gives a positive Fehling's solution test?
questions.explanation: Aliphatic aldehydes reduce Fehling's solution to red Cu₂O; aromatic aldehydes like benzaldehyde and ketones do not.

questions.question: Benzamide on treatment with Br₂ and aqueous NaOH (Hofmann bromamide degradation) gives
questions.explanation: Hofmann degradation removes the carbonyl carbon: C₆H₅CONH₂ → C₆H₅NH₂ (one carbon fewer).

questions.question: Which nitrogenous base is present in RNA but not in DNA?
questions.explanation: RNA contains uracil in place of thymine; adenine and cytosine occur in both.

questions.question: The monomer of natural rubber is
questions.explanation: Natural rubber is cis-1,4-polyisoprene (2-methylbuta-1,3-diene). Chloroprene gives neoprene.

questions.question: The molarity of a solution containing 4 g of NaOH dissolved in water to make 500 mL of solution is
questions.explanation: 4 g NaOH = 0.1 mol; molarity = 0.1/0.5 L = 0.2 M.

questions.question: The numbers of σ and π bonds in but-1-en-3-yne (CH₂=CH–C≡CH) are
questions.explanation: σ bonds: 4 C–H + 3 C–C = 7. π bonds: 1 in C=C and 2 in C≡C = 3.

questions.question: The negation of the statement 'All students are intelligent' is
questions.explanation: ¬(∀x p(x)) ≡ ∃x ¬p(x): there exists at least one student who is not intelligent.

questions.question: The inverse of the matrix A = [[2, 1], [5, 3]] (rows) is
The principal value of sin⁻¹(sin(5π/6)) is
questions.explanation: sin(5π/6) = 1/2 and the principal range of sin⁻¹ is [−π/2, π/2], so the value is π/6.

questions.question: The acute angle between the lines represented by x² − 4xy + y² = 0 is
The area of the triangle with vertices A(1, 1, 1), B(1, 2, 3) and C(2, 3, 1) is
The perpendicular distance of the point (2, 1, −1) from the plane x − 2y + 4z = 9 is
The angle between the line (x − 1)/2 = (y − 2)/1 = (z + 1)/(−2) and the plane x + y + 4z = 3 is
The maximum value of z = 3x + 2y subject to x + y ≤ 4, x ≤ 3, x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0 is
The derivative of xˣ at x = 1 is
questions.explanation: y = xˣ ⇒ dy/dx = xˣ(1 + ln x). At x = 1: 1 × (1 + 0) = 1.

questions.question: If x = a cos³t and y = a sin³t, then dy/dx equals
questions.explanation: dx/dt = −3a cos²t sin t, dy/dt = 3a sin²t cos t. dy/dx = −sin t/cos t = −tan t.

questions.question: The local minimum value of f(x) = x³ − 3x² + 4 is
∫ eˣ(1/x − 1/x²) dx equals
questions.explanation: Using ∫ eˣ(f(x) + f'(x)) dx = eˣf(x) + C with f(x) = 1/x and f'(x) = −1/x².

questions.question: The value of ∫ from 0 to π/2 of log(tan x) dx is
questions.explanation: Replacing x by π/2 − x turns log tan x into log cot x = −log tan x, so I = −I ⇒ I = 0.

questions.question: The area of the region bounded by the parabola y² = 4x and the line x = 1 is
The order and degree of the differential equation (d²y/dx²)³ + (dy/dx)⁴ + y = 0 are respectively
questions.explanation: Highest derivative is d²y/dx² (order 2), and its power is 3 (degree 3) since the equation is polynomial in derivatives.

questions.question: A random variable X takes values 0, 1, 2, 3 with probabilities k, 2k, 3k, 4k respectively. E(X) equals
A binomial random variable X has mean 4 and variance 3. Then P(X ≥ 1) is
The value of sin 75° is
The eccentricity of the ellipse 9x² + 16y² = 144 is
The modulus of (3 + 4i)/(1 − i) is
The period of a satellite revolving very close to the Earth’s surface is approximately (R = 6400 km, g = 10 m/s²)
A metal rod 1 m long expands by 0.6 mm when its temperature rises by 50 °C. The coefficient of linear expansion of the metal is
The radius of gyration of a uniform disc of radius R about a tangent lying in its plane is
questions.explanation: I = MR²/4 + MR² = 5MR²/4 = MK² ⇒ K = (√5/2)R.

questions.question: A small body tied to a string is whirled in a vertical circle of radius 1 m. The minimum speed it must have at the lowest point to just complete the circle is (g = 10 m/s²)
questions.explanation: Minimum speed at the top is √(gr); energy conservation gives v_bottom = √(5gr) = √50 ≈ 7.07 m/s. (√10 m/s is the minimum speed at the top.)

questions.question: A liquid rises to a height h in a capillary tube of radius r. In a tube of radius r/2 made of the same glass, the liquid will rise to a height
questions.explanation: h = 2T cos θ/(rρg) ∝ 1/r, so halving the radius doubles the rise.

questions.question: At what temperature will the rms speed of hydrogen molecules be equal to that of oxygen molecules at 320 K?
Two moles of an ideal gas expand isothermally and reversibly at 300 K to twice their initial volume. The work done by the gas is about (R = 8.314 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, ln 2 = 0.693)
The displacement of a particle in SHM is x = 5 sin(πt/3 + π/6) cm, with t in seconds. Its maximum speed is
questions.explanation: v_max = Aω = 5 × π/3 = 5π/3 cm/s ≈ 5.24 cm/s.

questions.question: The fundamental frequency of a pipe open at both ends is 300 Hz. If one end is closed, the fundamental frequency becomes
questions.explanation: Open pipe: f = v/2L; closed pipe: f = v/4L, i.e. half: 150 Hz.

questions.question: In Young’s double-slit experiment the slits are 1 mm apart and the screen is 1 m away. For light of wavelength 500 nm the fringe width is
A closed surface encloses charges of +3 μC, −5 μC and +4 μC. The net electric flux through the surface is (ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² C² N⁻¹ m⁻²)
questions.explanation: Net enclosed charge = +2 μC. φ = q/ε₀ = 2 × 10⁻⁶/8.85 × 10⁻¹² ≈ 2.26 × 10⁵ N m² C⁻¹. (1.36 × 10⁶ adds magnitudes.)

questions.question: A galvanometer of resistance 100 Ω gives full-scale deflection for 10 mA. The shunt needed to convert it into an ammeter of range 0–1 A is about
questions.explanation: S = I_g G/(I − I_g) = 0.01 × 100/0.99 ≈ 1.01 Ω, connected in parallel.

questions.topic: Magnetic Fields due to Electric Current
questions.question: A long solenoid has 1000 turns per metre and carries a current of 2 A. The magnetic field inside it is about (μ₀ = 4π × 10⁻⁷ T m/A)
The magnetic susceptibility of a paramagnetic substance is
options: small and negative, and independent of temperature
small and positive, and decreases as temperature increases
large and positive, and independent of temperature
small and positive, and increases with temperature
questions.explanation: Paramagnets have small positive χ obeying Curie’s law χ = C/T. Diamagnets have small negative, temperature-independent χ; ferromagnets have large positive χ.

questions.question: An inductor of self-inductance 0.5 H carries a steady current of 4 A. The energy stored in its magnetic field is
The capacitive reactance of a 10 μF capacitor in a 50 Hz AC circuit is about
A proton and an α-particle have the same kinetic energy. The ratio of their de Broglie wavelengths λ_p : λ_α is
questions.explanation: λ = h/√(2mK). With equal K, λ ∝ 1/√m: λ_p/λ_α = √(4m/m) = 2.

questions.question: The half-life of a radioactive substance is 20 days. The time taken for 75% of it to decay is
questions.explanation: 75% decayed means 25% = (1/2)² remains: 2 half-lives = 40 days.

questions.question: A Zener diode operated in reverse breakdown is mainly used as a
questions.explanation: In breakdown the Zener voltage stays nearly constant over a wide current range, so it regulates voltage.

questions.question: A uniform disc of moment of inertia 2 kg m² rotates freely at 10 rad/s about its axis. A small 1 kg lump of clay is gently stuck on it at 1 m from the axis. The new angular speed is
questions.explanation: Iω conserved: 2 × 10 = (2 + 1 × 1²)ω ⇒ ω = 20/3 ≈ 6.67 rad/s.

questions.question: A compound contains 40% carbon, 6.67% hydrogen and 53.33% oxygen by mass. Its empirical formula is
The hybridisation of carbon in diamond, graphite and ethyne is respectively
questions.explanation: Diamond: each C bonded tetrahedrally to 4 C (sp³). Graphite: trigonal planar layers (sp²). Ethyne: linear H–C≡C–H (sp).

questions.question: The IUPAC name of (CH₃)₂CH–CH₂–CH₂OH is
questions.explanation: Longest chain containing the –OH carbon has 4 carbons, numbered from the –OH end; the methyl group is on C-3: 3-methylbutan-1-ol.

questions.question: The number of atoms per unit cell of a face-centred cubic lattice is
questions.explanation: 8 corners × 1/8 + 6 face centres × 1/2 = 1 + 3 = 4.

questions.question: 3 g of urea (molar mass 60 g mol⁻¹) is dissolved in 500 g of water. The freezing point of the solution is (Kf of water = 1.86 K kg mol⁻¹)
questions.explanation: Molality = 0.05/0.5 = 0.1 m. ΔTf = 1.86 × 0.1 = 0.186 K, so the solution freezes at −0.186 °C.

questions.question: The solubility of BaSO₄ in water is 1 × 10⁻⁵ mol L⁻¹ at 298 K. Its solubility product is
questions.explanation: BaSO₄ ⇌ Ba²⁺ + SO₄²⁻; Ksp = s² = (10⁻⁵)² = 1 × 10⁻¹⁰. (4 × 10⁻¹⁵ would be 4s³ for an AB₂ salt.)

questions.question: Two moles of an ideal gas expand from 10 L to 20 L against a constant external pressure of 1 atm. The work done on the gas is (1 L atm = 101.3 J)
questions.explanation: W = −P_ext ΔV = −1 × (20 − 10) = −10 L atm = −1013 J (work done by the gas is +1013 J). The number of moles does not enter.

questions.question: A conductivity cell has a cell constant of 0.5 cm⁻¹. When filled with a solution its resistance is 100 Ω. The conductivity of the solution is
questions.explanation: κ = cell constant/R = 0.5/100 = 5 × 10⁻³ S cm⁻¹.

questions.question: The units of the rate constant of a second-order reaction are
questions.explanation: k = rate/[A]² ⇒ (mol L⁻¹ s⁻¹)/(mol L⁻¹)² = L mol⁻¹ s⁻¹. s⁻¹ is first order; mol L⁻¹ s⁻¹ zero order; L² mol⁻² s⁻¹ third order.

questions.question: Which halogen has the most negative electron gain enthalpy?
questions.explanation: Chlorine. Fluorine’s small 2p subshell causes strong electron–electron repulsion, so its electron gain enthalpy is less negative than chlorine’s.

questions.question: The shape of the XeF₄ molecule is
questions.explanation: Xe has 4 bond pairs and 2 lone pairs (sp³d², octahedral arrangement); the lone pairs are trans, giving a square planar shape.

questions.question: The most common oxidation state of the lanthanoids is
questions.explanation: All lanthanoids show the +3 state; +2 (Eu, Yb) and +4 (Ce) occur only for some elements.

questions.question: The effective atomic number (EAN) of iron in K₄[Fe(CN)₆] is
questions.explanation: Fe²⁺ has 26 − 2 = 24 electrons; six CN⁻ ligands donate 12 electrons: EAN = 36 (the krypton configuration).

questions.question: Which of the following alkyl bromides undergoes SN2 reaction fastest?
questions.explanation: SN2 requires backside attack; steric hindrance increases from methyl to 3°, so methyl bromide reacts fastest.

questions.question: tert-Butyl methyl ether is best prepared by Williamson synthesis from
questions.explanation: The alkyl halide must be primary (SN2). With tert-butyl bromide, the alkoxide acts as a base and gives 2-methylpropene by elimination.

questions.question: Which of the following is the strongest acid?
questions.explanation: Each Cl withdraws electron density (−I) and stabilises the carboxylate ion; trichloroacetic acid is the strongest.

questions.question: Aniline is treated with NaNO₂ and dilute HCl at 0–5 °C, and the solution is then warmed with water. The organic product is
questions.explanation: Diazotisation gives benzenediazonium chloride, which hydrolyses on warming with water to phenol with evolution of N₂.

questions.question: In sucrose, the two monosaccharide units are joined through
options: C-1 of α-D-glucose and C-4 of another glucose
C-1 of α-D-glucose and C-2 of β-D-fructose
C-1 of β-D-glucose and C-4 of β-D-galactose
C-2 of α-D-glucose and C-1 of β-D-fructose
questions.explanation: The glycosidic bond links the anomeric carbons C-1 of glucose and C-2 of fructose, so sucrose has no free reducing group.

questions.question: The monomer of nylon-6 is
questions.explanation: Nylon-6 is made by ring-opening polymerisation of caprolactam. Adipic acid + hexamethylenediamine give nylon-6,6; vinyl chloride gives PVC; chloroprene gives neoprene.

questions.question: A metal crystallises in a body-centred cubic lattice with an edge length of 300 pm. The atomic radius of the metal is about
questions.explanation: In bcc, atoms touch along the body diagonal: 4r = √3a ⇒ r = √3 × 300/4 ≈ 129.9 pm. (106.1 pm uses the fcc relation 4r = √2a.)

questions.question: The centre and radius of the circle x² + y² − 4x + 6y − 12 = 0 are
The number of diagonals of a decagon is
The variance of the observations 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 is
questions.explanation: Mean = 6; squared deviations 16, 4, 0, 4, 16 sum to 40; variance = 40/5 = 8.

questions.question: The value of lim (x → 0) (eˣ − 1 − x)/x² is
Which of the following statement patterns is a tautology?
questions.explanation: (p ∧ q) → p is false only if p ∧ q is true and p false, which is impossible. p → (p ∧ q) fails for p = T, q = F; (p ∨ q) → p fails for p = F, q = T.

questions.question: The converse of the statement ‘If it rains, then the match is cancelled’ is
options: If it does not rain, then the match is not cancelled.
If the match is cancelled, then it rains.
If the match is not cancelled, then it does not rain.
It rains and the match is not cancelled.
questions.explanation: The converse of p → q is q → p. The others are the inverse, the contrapositive and the negation respectively.

questions.question: The adjoint of A = [[1, 2], [3, 4]] (rows) is
questions.explanation: For [[a, b], [c, d]], adj = [[d, −b], [−c, a]] = [[4, −2], [−3, 1]]. [[4, −3], [−2, 1]] is the cofactor matrix before transposing.

questions.question: The general solution of tan θ = √3 is
questions.explanation: tan θ = tan(π/3) ⇒ θ = nπ + π/3 (tan has period π).

questions.question: The lines represented by 3x² + 2hxy + 3y² = 0 are coincident. Then h equals
questions.explanation: Coincident lines require h² = ab = 9 ⇒ h = ±3.

questions.question: The volume of the parallelepiped with coterminous edges î + 2ĵ + 3k̂, ĵ + 2k̂ and î + k̂ is
The equation of the plane passing through (1, 2, 3) and perpendicular to the vector 2î − ĵ + k̂ is
The minimum value of z = 2x + 3y subject to x + y ≥ 4, x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0 is
questions.explanation: The feasible region is unbounded with corner points (4, 0) and (0, 4): z = 8 and 12. Since 2x + 3y < 8 has no point in the region, the minimum is 8.

questions.question: For |x| < 1, the derivative of tan⁻¹(2x/(1 − x²)) with respect to x is
questions.explanation: With x = tan θ, the expression equals 2θ = 2 tan⁻¹ x for |x| < 1, so the derivative is 2/(1 + x²).

questions.question: The slope of the normal to the curve y = x³ − 2x at the point (1, −1) is
questions.explanation: dy/dx = 3x² − 2 = 1 at x = 1 (slope of tangent), so the normal has slope −1.

questions.question: ∫ x eˣ dx equals
questions.explanation: By parts: x eˣ − ∫eˣ dx = (x − 1)eˣ + C.

questions.question: The value of ∫ from 0 to π/2 of sin⁴x/(sin⁴x + cos⁴x) dx is
questions.explanation: Using x → π/2 − x, I equals the same integral with cos⁴x on top; adding, 2I = π/2, so I = π/4.

questions.question: The area enclosed by the ellipse x²/16 + y²/9 = 1 is
questions.explanation: Area = πab = π × 4 × 3 = 12π.

questions.question: The general solution of dy/dx = (1 + y²)/(1 + x²) is
questions.explanation: Separating variables: dy/(1 + y²) = dx/(1 + x²) ⇒ tan⁻¹y = tan⁻¹x + c.

questions.question: A continuous random variable X has probability density function f(x) = kx² for 0 ≤ x ≤ 3 and 0 otherwise. The value of k is
questions.explanation: ∫₀³ kx² dx = 9k = 1 ⇒ k = 1/9.

questions.question: For a binomial distribution with n = 10 and p = 0.4, the variance is
questions.explanation: Variance = npq = 10 × 0.4 × 0.6 = 2.4 (the mean is 4).
